f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.name: Dagger
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.author: Huda Kilani
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.materials: Silver, iron; casting, incised and niello
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.description2: Silver knife with silver handle and niello decoration on the front; metal on the backside and four Turkish coins along the edge of the sheath; a name (‘Jomaah Ali’) is inscribed on the blade of the dagger. This object is functional and can be used in everyday activities, but at the same time it is a prestigious object that every Bedouin man must have. The most common types of daggers in Jordan are the Yemeni dagger, the Hijazi and other local types.

f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.name: Cross chain
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.author: Huda Kilani
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.description2: A cross of silver on a silver chain known with the folkloric name “heal of gazelle”, worn by Christian women. Silver was the most common jewellery; only rich people used gold. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated religious composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.name: *Théâtre du Châtelet. Germinal*
f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.description2: The thirteenth novel in the *Rougon-Macquart* series, *Germinal* (1885), is the most well-known and the most discussed of Zola's works. This naturalist writer took a new approach to depicting workers' lives, shedding light on miners' terrible working conditions and the violence and difficulty of strikes. Fearing that the adaptation of this novel for stage would trigger social unrest, the play was initially banned. It was finally performed for the first time in 1888 at the Théâtre du Châtelet. This poster highlights the most important themes of the novel - life in the mine, strikes, etc.

fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.name: Celebrations for the 50 years of the Female Workers Friendly Society of Pavia (Italy), and inauguration of a new standard
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.author: Angela Bellardi
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.archival: ASCr, Società di mutuo soccorso femminile di Cremona
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.third_name: *Festa cinquantenaria della Società operaia femminile di M. S. Inaugurazione del vessillo sociale. Madrina S.E. Donna Elena Cairoli. Padrino Ill. Sig. Comm Franchi-Maggi*
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.description2: During the second half of the 19th century, “friendly societies” flourished in Italy (especially in Central and Northern Italy). They predated trade unionism and were an important element of Italian social life. From this picture we can infer that the Female Workers Friendly Society of Pavia had been created in 1854.

fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.name: Madrasa Slimaniya
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.history: The *madarasa* has many functions, combining prayer with education and providing accommodation for students who have come to the capital to pursue their studies. The role of the *madrasa* in the medina was important not only for spreading knowledge, but also for enabling social mobility by providing education free of charge. The Husainid princes built a great number of madrasas in the city.
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.description2: Located in the medina on the eponymous street, the Madrasa al-Slimaniya was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey in memory of his son, Sliman. Architecturally, it is can be distinguished by its great elevated porch resting on columns which are topped by Turkish capitals, crowning a green-tiled cornice. The square-shaped oratory is covered in barrel vaults and the walls are decorated with ceramic tiles and panels. The beautiful carved stucco, as well as the elegant dome and the beauty of the *mihrab*, make the Slimanya oratory one of the most magnificent *madrasas* in Tunisia.

fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.name: Hôpital Charles Nicolle
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.history: The first great hospital to be built following the establishment of the protectorate, the Hôpital Charles Nicolle initially accepted only French patients. Having been established initially by a beylical decree on 9 June 1897, it was renamed after the doctor Charles Nicolle, the director of l'Institut Pasteur in Tunis from 1903 to 1936 and 1928 Nobel Prize for Physiology winner, in 1944. The Hôpital Charles Nicolle became known for its pioneering work and specialism in virologic diagnosis, congenital illnesses and paediatric nephrology.
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.keywords: Charles Nicolle; Institut Pasteur; Nobel prize
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.description2: This hospital was built over 12 hectares, at the foot of the Rabta Hill just outside the ramparts of the city. It was designed by the architect Resplandy, with the help of Dr Bastide. The hospital initially provided two different kinds of general medicine services and surgery, and had 190 beds. Two more buildings were added during the 20th century. Today, the Hôpital Charles Nicolle is a renowned university hospital.

fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.name: Photo showing the Institute of Medicine
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.keywords: Faculty; Medicine; Pharmacy; USJ; SJU; University; Education
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.description2: The Medical school at the Université Saint Joseph (USJ) was established by the French state in 1883. The French state provided funding, a curriculum, and professors. Later that same year, following an agreement between the Jesuits and the French government, the Institute of Medicine opened on the university's campus. This was later followed by the opening of many other institutes, such as the faculties of law, economics and management, and literature. On 6 October 1888, the French government recognized the institute as part of a Faculty of Medicine. In 1889, when the school of pharmacy was founded, it was renamed as the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy.

fdae7b92-4bc6-5157-9b5e-a4cfe7c51307.name: *The Ambulance*
fdae7b92-4bc6-5157-9b5e-a4cfe7c51307.description2: Sava Henţia was a Romanian painter who studied in Rome and Paris. During the Romanian Independence War (the Russian-Ottoman war of 1877–1878), he was one of the four Romanian painters who accompanied the Romanian army on the front with the purpose of depicting scenes from the war. However, he did not only dedicate himself to painting, but also worked as a volunteer for the Romanian Ambulance Service. In the foreground of the painting The Ambulance, some Romanian doctors are attending Ottoman soldiers, while in the background can be seen medical tents of the Red Cross.
